alt: Four factors help wayfinding: directional and identification signs, aligned "you are here" maps at entrances and junctions, landmarks and a simple layout, and familiarity. A schematic contrasts an aligned map, where up means straight ahead, with one that is not aligned. Dogu and Erkip (2000) surveyed shoppers in one mall.
caption: Signs, aligned maps, landmarks and familiarity all help shoppers find their way.

alt: Four schematic store plans: a short trip enters, visits one area and leaves; a round trip follows the outer edge; a central trip goes through the central aisles; a wave trip zig-zags up and down the aisles. Five spatial behaviour patterns range from focused specialist and native visits, through broad tourist and explorer routes, to fast raider visits. Gil et al. (2009) tracked routes by CCTV.
caption: Trip types describe routes; spatial patterns describe styles of shopping.

alt: Two schematic menus: a positive one with clear categories and a boxed, highlighted item, and a negative one with prices in a neat column that invites comparing by price. Lists of positive features (highlighting, clear categories, accurate descriptions, readable font) and negative features (price column, too many items, clutter) follow; eye-tracking can test them objectively.
caption: Highlight what you want to sell; do not line prices up for comparison.

alt: A menu category of five items: the first and last are chosen more often than the same items in the middle, matching primacy and recency effects in which first and last items get more attention and are better remembered.
caption: Put the dishes you want to sell first or last in a category.

after: ### Hall's four zones and the functions of personal space
alt: Three functions of personal space: overload (keeping distance reduces overwhelming stimulation), arousal (closeness is pleasant with a partner, unpleasant with strangers) and behaviour constraint (others too close limit freedom to talk or move). Applied to close restaurant tables, overheard conversations and limits on what diners say explain why the romantic scenario was most affected.
caption: Distance protects us from overload, unwanted arousal and constraint.

after: ### Defending a place in a queue
alt: A schematic queue: an intruder steps in with a brief neutral comment; people directly behind the intrusion point object most, those in front less. Two intruders caused more objection than one; passive buffers behind the intruder reduced objection; responses were mostly verbal, physical action rare. Real queues give ecological validity but raise ethical and cultural issues.
caption: People who lost their place objected most; buffers took the pressure off.
